why: Non-self-opened answers are in the plain mode, whose accuracy (implied by 224/500 = s*0.82 + (1-s)*a with s about 0.34) is about 0.26-0.30 whatever later 'Wait'/'Hmm' markers appear, while the cued base is right about 0.75-0.80 on these somewhat harder problems.

The mode is fixed at the opening and nothing after it adds accuracy, so within plain-mode answers a later self-check marker gives about no gain, minus a little because those answers fall on longer, harder problems.

On the 328, plain 76/328 and cue 164/328 imply a plain-mode accuracy of about 0.12 against about 0.45 for the cue on the harder problems where plain answers show self-check markers; later markers don't shift the mode.
